tests.procedure: Under strong white light, check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and compliance with the visual specifications.

details.reference: BP 2024 (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs; BP 2024 Monograph for Sucrose

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg of sample in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL of the solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 +/- 0.5 C for 15 min (repeat if not dissolved); stepwise add 0.9 mL, 2 mL and 7 mL of solvent (same shake and hold) to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved, 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble.

details.solventsNote: solvents as stated in the spec sheet row

tests.procedure: IR: examine the spectrum obtained for the sample and compare it with the spectrum obtained from Sucrose CRS.

Dilute 1 mL of solution S to 100 mL with water. To 5 mL add 0.15 mL freshly prepared copper sulfate solution and 2 mL dilute sodium hydroxide; solution is blue and clear and remains so after boiling. Add 4 mL dilute hydrochloric acid to the hot solution, boil 1 min, then add 4 mL dilute sodium hydroxide. An orange precipitate is formed immediately.

details.solutionS: 50.0 g in water, diluted to 100 mL (STM Prepared reagents)

tests.procedure: TLC on silica gel plate. Test solution: 10 mg in 2 volumes water and 3 volumes methanol, diluted to 20 mL. Reference (a): 10 mg sucrose CRS in same solvent mixture. Reference (b): 10 mg each of fructose, glucose, lactose monohydrate and sucrose in same mixture. Mobile phase: cold saturated boric acid solution, 60 % V/V glacial acetic acid, anhydrous ethanol, acetone, ethyl acetate (10:15:20:60:60 V/V/V/V/V). Apply 2 µL; develop in unsaturated tank over 3/4 of plate; dry in warm air; spray with 0.5 g thymol in 5 mL sulfuric acid and 95 mL ethanol (96 per cent); heat at 130 C for 10 min. System suitability: reference (b) shows 4 clearly separated spots. The principal spot of the test solution is similar in position, colour and size to that of reference (a).
To a sufficient amount of solution S, compare the clarity of the sample with water. Solution S is clear.

details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix IV A (Clarity of Solution)

tests.procedure: Dissolve 31.3 g in CO2-free water (from distilled water) and dilute to 100 mL. Measure the conductivity of the solution (C1) and of the water used (C2) with a calibrated conductivity meter, stirring gently; readings must be stable within 1 % over 30 s. Calculate conductivity of the substance with the expression in the STM (expression not shown in the text, see openQuestions).
Dissolve 26.0 g in water and dilute to 100.0 mL with the same solvent. Measure with a calibrated polarimeter.

details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix V F (Determination of Optical Rotation and Specific Optical Rotation)

tests.procedure: To 5 mL of solution S add 5 mL water, 1.0 mL of 1 M sodium hydroxide and 1.0 mL of 1 g/L methylene blue. Mix, place in water-bath; after exactly 2 min remove and examine immediately. The blue colour must not disappear completely; ignore blue colour at the air/solution interface.

Dissolve 50.0 g in 50.0 mL water; mix; filter (0.45 µm pores); degas. Measure absorbance at 420 nm, minimum path length 4 cm (10 cm or more preferred). Calculate the colour value with the expression in the STM (expression not shown in the text, see openQuestions). The STM also says 'Mix and place in a water-bath' (no purpose stated).

details.concentrationNote: from refractive index, Table 0204.-1 (interpolate if necessary)
details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix II B (UV-Visible); BP 2024 Appendix V E (Refractive Index)

tests.procedure: Test solution: 4.0 g sample in freshly prepared distilled water diluted to 10.0 mL. Reference solution: 4.0 g sample + 0.5 mL sulfite standard solution (80 ppm SO2) diluted to 10.0 mL. Blank: distilled water. Take 2.0 mL each in 10 mm cuvettes; add kit reagents; measure absorbance at about 340 nm before and at end of reaction; subtract blank. The absorbance difference of the test solution must not be greater than half that of the reference solution.

details.criterion: absorbance difference of test not greater than half that of reference
details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix II B (UV-Visible); BP 2024 Monograph for Sucrose

tests.procedure: Weigh a previously dried (105 C) weighing bottle (W0); weigh 2.000 g sample into it (W1); dry in calibrated oven at 105 C for 3 h, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2); repeat to constant weight. % LOD = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.
